definitions: In computer programming, the scope of a variable or function is determined by its position within the source code at the time of definition, rather than at the time of execution.
A scoping mechanism where the visibility of variables is determined by the physical placement of code blocks within the program.
examples: Understanding lexical scope is crucial for predicting how variables will behave in closures.
JavaScript primarily uses lexical scope, which can sometimes be confusing for beginners.
The function captured the variable from its lexical scope.
